messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected: continuous-batcher pool (us-east-1) high P95/P99 latency + repeated GPU OOMs. auto-escalation triggered. link: https://internal.incidents/2432109876 :rotating_light:

jamie: seeing a spike around 22:17 UTC, node group cb-east-4 showing multiple container restarts

sasha: logs show repeated allocation failures and then kernel page faults on nvme-backed nodes. stack traces include runtime::BatchAccumulator::grow()

anil: customer reports 502s from hosted API — looks correlated. which tenants impacted? support-bot, any alerts?

support-bot: @carla impacted customers: alpha-pay, docs-search-prod. error rate up 9x for alpha-pay since 22:18 UTC. SLA risk for dedicated customers.

carla: passing to CSMs. we need ETA and mitigation, please prioritize

jamie: hypothesize: continuous batching growth loop + KV cache pressure -> huge memory footprint -> GPU OOM -> container crash -> node kubelet restarts restarting many pods -> convergence/queue pileup -> further growth.

infra-bot: node flaps detected on i-0a9* in cb-east-4: 3 nodes re-provisioned in 7m. kernel messages: "OOM killer invoked" and "page allocation failure"

anil: can someone pull a heap snapshot from a crashed container? if not, collect dmesg + nvidia-smi logs from node.

jamie: collecting nvidia-smi before node reclaim, attaching recent sample: ```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1
+----------------------+
| memory.used [MiB]   |
+----------------------+
| 15360 MiB           |
| 15360 MiB           |
| 15360 MiB           |
```

sasha: also saw long tail latency in batch assembly: single batch growing to 15k tokens, KV cache retention skyrocketing. suggests accumulator not respecting max_batch_tokens under load.

jamie: temporary mitigation options: 1) enable emergency throttle on continuous-batcher route (reduce max inflight), 2) flip feature flag to disable continuous batching on effected pool, 3) scale up and cordon problematic nodes to stop noisy tenants. Which do we want now?

anil: flip FF for continuous batching on cb-east-4 for all non-dedicated tiers. That will reduce throughput but should stop growth loop. jamie, can you run the flag?

jamie: running: ```./ffctl set continuous_batching cb-east-4 false --scope=hosted --reason="emergency: OOM/paging"``` applying now...

ops-bot: FLAG change recorded: continuous_batching disabled on cb-east-4 (hosted) by jamie.

sasha: starting to see drops in batch sizes at 22:25 UTC. backlog decreasing but some nodes still restart. CPU page faults persist on nodes with older kernel.

carla: alpha-pay error rate down to 2.1x baseline. support updated customers with temporary degraded throughput notice.

anil: we should push a short-term hotfix to enforce absolute max_batch_tokens at the runtime level even if FF enabled. jamie, can we hotpatch?

jamie: building patch branch: runtime: enforce hard cap at allocator level (commit: a1b2c3d). test on staging now. CI green for smoke.

ops-bot: deploy started to cb-east-4-canary (1 pod). rolling to remainder on success.

sasha: while canary is up, observing reduced page fault counts. suspect kernel CVE-ish memory allocator interaction when page cache spikes. need follow-up with eng-runtime to audit growth paths.

jamie: can we cordon two noisy nodes to stop further flapping while we deploy? infra-bot, cordon request:
```kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-12 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30```

infra-bot: cordon + drain executed on ip-10-0-45-12 and ip-10-0-45-19. Pods redistributed. No failures during drain.

anil: if hotfix is safe, let's promote. Also open a post-incident ticket to investigate continuous batching accumulator edge case: potential unbounded growth when KV cache hits > X and backlog > Y. Add load-tests reproducer.

jamie: promote patch to cb-east-4 production. rollout completed at 22:38 UTC, restart count stabilizing.

ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. root cause: unbounded batch accumulation interacting with KV/paging causing memory pressure -> GPU OOM -> node flaps. Impact: elevated latency and 5xxs for some hosted tenants for ~20 minutes. Severity: SEV2.

carla: customers notified with postmortem note: temporary flag disable + narrow runtime cap applied.

sasha: follow-ups: 1) add hard caps in runtime (done), 2) add telemetry for batch size distribution per route, 3) add preemptive node-level OOM alerts, 4) reproduce in chaos testing with KV cache thrash. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

anil: creating incident task list and assigning owners. ETA for full root cause analysis and permanent fix: 5 business days.

jamie: leaving on-call notes: commands run, patches, nodes cordoned, customers and support updated. handing off to night on-call @sasha. :handshake:

sasha: taking over. monitoring for 2h. will escalate if new flaps occur.

support-bot: Customer update sent to alpha-pay and docs-search-prod. follow-up scheduled.
summary: Emergency on-call thread: continuous-batcher unbounded growth -> KV/paging pressure -> GPU OOMs -> node flaps. Temporary disable of continuous batching; runtime hard-cap hotfix deployed; cordoned nodes; incident mitigated. Follow-ups assigned.
